item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J02275","case1_error":"Treats 70% cheaper as paying 70% of the original price instead of 30%.","case2_error":"Correctly finds 10 cakes remaining, then reports 50 cakes already baked as the number still needed.","reason":"Case 1 misinterprets a percentage discount; case 2 answers the complementary quantity after correctly calculating the requested remainder.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02276","case1_error":"Uses purchase cost per egg instead of the stated selling price to calculate sales needed to recover capital.","case2_error":"Subtracts coupon savings from the discounted payment instead of adding them back; also labels a dollar amount as cents.","reason":"Case 1 substitutes the wrong unit price; case 2 reverses discount reconstruction and mishandles units. Its conflicting answer marker does not erase these explicit errors.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02277","case1_error":"Reduces the required rope length by 25% instead of accounting for lost usable length in the purchased rope.","case2_error":"Treats 10 hours over five days as 10 hours per day, omitting division by five.","reason":"Case 1 applies loss to the requirement in the wrong direction; case 2 mistakes a multiday total for a daily rate.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02278","case1_error":"No clear mathematical error: correctly reports 4 movies and 16 books; the question permits separate counts.","case2_error":"Subtracts a pool fraction directly from liters without conversion and incorrectly concludes that all 120 liters remain.","reason":"Case 1 reasonably answers the question despite the reference preferring a combined total, so both cases do not have diagnosable errors.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J02279","case1_error":"Subtracts car expenses from the console price as though they were available savings, ignoring the calculated earnings balance.","case2_error":"Treats pay cut to 75% as a reduction by 75%, leaving 25% instead.","reason":"Case 1 confuses spent money with funds available toward a purchase; case 2 confuses the retained percentage with the percentage removed.","judgment":"different"}]}
